title: Make the GitHub repo public + enable branch protection
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)
The repo `jimbottle/just-my-weather` is **private** (`gh repo view` → `"visibility":"PRIVATE"`), but everything shipped for open-sourcing it — LICENSE (Apache-2.0), README with a CI badge, CONTRIBUTING, docs/, and .github/ issue+PR templates — only has effect once the repo is public. Flipping visibility and setting repo policy is an owner-only action: it needs GitHub account authority I don't have, it's a deliberate/consequential publish decision (public history is hard to fully retract), and there's no code workaround. I've done all the in-repo prep; only the GitHub-side switch remains.

## Steps
1. Confirm you actually want this public now (pre-1.0, versionName 0.1.0). If not, tell me and I'll leave it private and drop the CI badge.
2. Make it public: GitHub → repo **Settings → General → Danger Zone → Change visibility → Public** (or `gh repo edit jimbottle/just-my-weather --visibility public`).
3. (Recommended) Protect `main`: Settings → **Branches → Add branch ruleset/protection** for `main` → require the **CI** status check to pass before merge, and require a PR. The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) is already green on main.
4. (Optional) Verify the README CI badge renders and the issue/PR templates appear when opening a new issue/PR.
5. Close this issue when done.

## What unblocks me when this returns
Just the repo being public (and, if you did step 3, branch protection on). Nothing in the codebase depends on it — this is purely the GitHub-side publish. If you decide NOT to go public, say so here and I'll revert the CI badge and adjust the README's open-source framing.

title: Alerting: precip-probability forecast rules ('rain within N hours')
description: Forecast-window alerting (xpp) shipped temperature/wind windows (overnight low, frost, heat/wind ahead) because the ForecastPoint domain model only carries temperature and wind. 'Rain starting within N hours' needs precipitation probability from the hourly forecast: extend NwsWire/NwsModels ForecastPoint with probabilityOfPrecipitation, parse it in NwsClient.getHourlyForecast, add a PRECIP_PROBABILITY concept (it isn't one of the current observation WeatherFields), and a rule shape for 'precip probability above X% within window' (or first-hour-of-rain). Distinct evaluation from the min/max-extreme path. Builds on AlertWindow + AlertEvaluator's forecast path already in place.
close_reason: Shipped precip-chance forecast alerts. ForecastPoint+probabilityOfPrecipitation parsed; new sealed AlertSubject (WeatherField | PrecipChance) replaces AlertRule.field — precip is forecast-only (kept out of the view catalog), rides the max-over-window path. Codec back-compat via legacy 'field' key. Builder offers rain only under forecast windows. Verified on device.

title: Alerting: forecast-window & overnight-low rules
description: Beyond current-observation thresholds: 'rain starting within N hours', 'overnight low below X', frost risk — using getHourlyForecast (already ported). Builds on AlertRule with a time window + forecast evaluation path.
close_reason: Shipped forecast-window alerting (AlertWindow: overnight + next 6/12/24h) with pure forecast evaluation path, worker wiring, persistence, and builder UI. Temperature/wind windows cover overnight-low/frost/heat/wind-ahead; precip-probability rules split to just-my-weather-x5p. Verified on device.

title: Alerting: tone & frequency controls
description: Per-rule or global controls for how loud/often: quiet hours, sound/vibration on/off (extra channels), snooze, and polling cadence. v1 ships one default channel and a fixed 1h cadence.
close_reason: Shipped quiet hours (v1 of tone/frequency): global AlertSettings (quietHoursEnabled + window, isQuietAt wraps midnight) persisted via DataStore; AlertNotifier gained a low-importance silent channel; the worker delivers on it during quiet hours so overnight alerts arrive hushed, not dropped. Alerts screen toggle. Remaining knobs (custom window, per-rule tone/snooze, cadence) split to just-my-weather-pcj/-ken. Verified on device.

close_reason: Delivered + verified on Pixel_7_API_34: AlertRule + pure AlertEvaluator, DataStore persistence with firing-state dedup, AlertNotifier + personal-alerts channel, periodic + launch AlertWorker, Alerts screen + rule builder. title: Saved/named locations + place picker
description: The app currently shows the device's coarse location or falls back to WeatherLocation.DEFAULT (New York); there's no way to pick or save a named place, and the README overstated this ('set a place by hand'). Add the ability to choose/save one or more places. OPEN DESIGN QUESTION for a human: how to enter a place given the app's ethos (no Play Services, no API key, builds from source)? Options: (a) raw lat/lon entry, (b) a bundled US city list, (c) an external geocoder (adds a key/dependency — likely against the ethos). NWS has no geocoding. Was the remaining scope of the closed iy0 persistence epic.

title: Alerting: configurable polling cadence
description: t59 v1 keeps the fixed 1h periodic worker. Let the user choose cadence (e.g. 30m/1h/3h/6h); feed it into AlertWorker.schedule's PeriodicWorkRequest interval, persisted in AlertSettings. Mind WorkManager's 15m minimum.
close_reason: Configurable polling cadence shipped: AlertSettings.pollMinutes (30m/1h/3h/6h) persisted; AlertWorker.schedule parameterized + uses UPDATE so a cadence change retunes the periodic worker while an unchanged interval keeps its schedule; 'Check every' chip row on the Alerts screen. Verified on device: chips persist across relaunch and the worker stays ENQUEUED through the retune.

title: Alerting: custom quiet-hours window + per-rule tone/snooze

title: Schedule alert worker only when rules exist
description: Optimization: cancel the periodic AlertWorker when the rule list becomes empty and (re)schedule when the first rule is added, instead of always-on KEEP. Saves the hourly no-op wake on quiet installs.
close_reason: Periodic alert worker now scheduled only when an enabled rule exists. AlertWorker.sync()/cancel(); AlertsViewModel re-syncs on every edit (onRulesChanged); onCreate schedules only if rules are live. Verified via WorkManager diagnostics: personal-alerts CANCELLED with no rules, ENQUEUED after adding one.
